To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GABAergic amacrine neurons in rat retina receive synaptic input from bipolar cells and GABAergic amacine cells and make synaptic output onto bipolar cells and GAD‐negative and GAD‐ positive amacrine cells.

GABAergic cells in rat retina are amacrine cells, and that these cells are presynaptic in conventional synapses onto ganglion cells and bipolar cells, and in reciprocal synapses with bipolar cells, and postsynaptic to bipolar cells in reciprocal synapses.

GABAergic neurons in rat retina are located in the inner and outer portions of the inner nuclear and ganglion cell layers and that they are presynaptic elements in conventional synapses with bipolar and amacrine cells and with ganglion cells, as well as in synaptic dyads and probable reciprocal synapses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a group of GABA‐containing amacrine cells in the mammalian retina.
the identification of the neurotransmitter GABA in the mammalian retina and with an investigation of its role in the visual process.
the synaptic organization and connectivity of GABA‐synthesis amacrine cells in the mammalian retina.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GABAergic cells in the rat retina are amacrine cells which form reciprocal synaptic dyads with bipolar cells and serial synapses onto amacrine and ganglion cell dendrites.

GAD‐positive amacrine cells in the rat retina receive synaptic input from bipolar cells and from other GAD ‐positive cells, and that they make synapses on bipolar and amacrine cells, on ganglion cells, on other GAD‐ positive cells, and on themselves.
GAD‐positive amacrine cells receive most of their input from bipolar cells, and that they make synaptic contact with most of the other retinal neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GABAergic amacrine neurons are the major source of GABA in the rat retina and that they form a complex synaptic circuitry with other retinal neurons.
there are two types of GABAergic neurons in rat retina: a large population of amacrine cells and a smaller population of bipolar cells.
the GAD‐positive neurons of rat retina are a diverse population of amacrine cells which are the principal inhibitory elements in the inner retina.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GABA‐containing neurons are a heterogeneous population of amacrine cells that form a complex synaptic network in the IPL.
there is a population of GABAergic amacrine cell in rat retina that is functionally and morphologically similar to the AII cells of rabbit and other species.

there are two distinct populations of GABAergic amacrine neurons in the rat retina: (1) a small population of amacrine cells that receive synaptic input from bipolar and amacrine cells but do not form synapses with other amacrine or ganglion cells and (2) a much larger population of amacrine neurons that receive synaptic input only from bipolar cells and that form reciprocal and serial synapses as well as synaptic dyads with other amacrine and ganglion cells.
